No signal handler is registered (no signal/sigaction symbols in the binary), so the default action terminates the process.
source.description: eval_expr tokenizes the attacker-controlled expression string. If the divisor is zero, idiv raises #DE -> SIGFPE -> process death. The attacker directly controls the divisor value via literal tokens (e.g., '0' or '0x0' pushes zero onto the stack). The crash occurs before any push of the result or any printf output, so no memory corruption or info leak occurs — only process termination.

verification_plan.method: Send a division-by-zero expression ('1 0 /') to the target binary via stdin. Observe process termination with SIGFPE (signal 8, return code -8). Use GDB to confirm the fault occurs at the idiv instruction (eval_expr+0xc7 / link-time 0x1497) with divisor [rbp-0x18]=0. Test multiple input variants (decimal, hex, different dividends) to confirm reproducibility.
verification_plan.environment: Linux x86-64, Ubuntu GLIBC 2.39, PIE binary with Canary, NX, Partial RELRO, CET IBT+SHSTK enabled
expected_evidence: GDB: breakpoint at eval_expr+0xc7 (0x1497) hits before crash
Multiple input variants (decimal/hex) all reproduce SIGFPE

mitigations.name: NX (Non-Executable Stack)
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant to this primitive. SIGFPE is a CPU arithmetic exception, not a code execution vector. NX does not prevent or mitigate the crash.

mitigations.name: Canary (Stack Protector)
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. The crash occurs via a CPU exception (idiv by zero), not via stack buffer overflow. Canary does not prevent SIGFPE.

mitigations.name: PIE / ASLR
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. The crash is deterministic regardless of base address. The idiv instruction always faults on zero divisor at the same link-time offset.

mitigations.name: Partial RELRO
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. This primitive does not involve GOT or any memory write. It is a pure CPU exception.

mitigations.name: CET (IBT + SHSTK)
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. CET protects against ROP/COP via indirect branch tracking and shadow stack. SIGFPE is a synchronous CPU exception, not a control-flow hijack.

mitigations.name: alarm(60)
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. The crash is immediate (sub-second). alarm(60) would only trigger after 60 seconds of inactivity, which never occurs.

evidence.description: Division operator handler disassembly: at 0x1439 cmp eax,0x2f ('/') -> je 0x1491. At 0x1491: mov rax,[rbp-0x10] (load dividend); 0x1495: cqo (sign-extend rax into rdx:rax); 0x1497: idiv QWORD PTR [rbp-0x18] (divide by divisor). No test/cmp/jcc on [rbp-0x18] before idiv. If [rbp-0x18]==0, CPU raises #DE -> SIGFPE.

Operator handling: at 0x141e call pop (pop b = divisor -> [rbp-0x18]); at 0x142c call pop (pop a = dividend -> [rbp-0x10]). The divisor comes from the first pop, which returns either an attacker-pushed literal or underflowed memory. The attacker directly controls whether 0 is on the stack via the '0' or '0x0' literal token.

No signal() or sigaction() symbols found in the binary (nm filter for 'signal' and 'sigaction' returned no output). This confirms no SIGFPE handler is registered, so the default action (process termination) applies.

GDB breakpoint at eval_expr+0xc7 (link-time 0x1497, the idiv instruction) hit with input '1 0 /'. Register state: rax=0x1 (dividend), rdx=0x0 (cqo sign-extension). Stack: [rbp-0x18]=0x0000000000000000 (divisor=zero), [rbp-0x10]=0x0000000000000001 (dividend=1). This confirms the idiv is about to execute with a zero divisor.

GDB crash analysis: signal=SIGFPE (Arithmetic exception), crash_addr=0x0000555555555497 (PIE runtime address = link-time 0x1497 + PIE base). Backtrace: #0 eval_expr, #1 main. Process terminated by SIGFPE.

PoC execution: 4 input variants all produced rc=-8 (SIGFPE): '1 0 /' (decimal), '5 0 /' (decimal), '0x1 0x0 /' (hex), '100 0 /' (decimal). All variants confirm reproducible process termination via SIGFPE.

verification_result.details: GDB confirmed: breakpoint at eval_expr+0xc7 (0x1497) hit before crash. Divisor [rbp-0x18]=0x0 (zero), dividend [rbp-0x10]=0x1. idiv with zero divisor raises SIGFPE. No signal handler registered -> process terminated. PoC tested 4 input variants (decimal/hex), all reproduced rc=-8 (SIGFPE). The crash occurs at the idiv instruction before any push(result) or printf output, so no memory corruption or info leak occurs — pure DOS/CRASH primitive.

primitives.notes: BUG-002 produces a single DIRECT CRASH primitive. The idiv instruction faults synchronously on zero divisor before any memory write (push at 0x149e is never reached) or any output (printf in main is never reached). Therefore no higher-order primitive (ARB_WRITE, INFO_LEAK, RIP_CONTROL) can be derived from this BUG alone. The primitive is purely a denial-of-service: the attacker can terminate the calculator process on demand by sending a division-by-zero expression. The attack cost is minimal: a 6-byte expression string ('1 0 /') within the 1023-byte input limit. No preconditions beyond sending the expression are required. The primitive is trivially reproducible and deterministic.

non_primitives.reason: The idiv instruction at 0x1497 faults synchronously on zero divisor before the push(result) at 0x149e is reached. No memory write occurs. The division result is never computed or pushed. Therefore no write primitive of any kind (ARB_WRITE, RELATIVE_WRITE, RESTRICTED_WRITE) can be derived from BUG-002.

The SIGFPE crash terminates the process inside eval_expr before control returns to main. The printf('Result: %lld') in main (at 0x163b) is never reached. No output beyond the banner/prompt is produced. Therefore no information leak primitive can be derived from BUG-002.

SIGFPE is a synchronous CPU exception (arithmetic trap), not a control-flow hijack. The CPU raises #DE and the kernel delivers SIGFPE with default action (terminate). There is no mechanism by which the zero divisor value influences the instruction pointer. The fault address is always the idiv instruction (0x1497), not an attacker-controlled address. Therefore no RIP_CONTROL or FUNCTION_POINTER_CONTROL primitive can be derived from BUG-002.

BUG-002 involves no heap operations. The idiv instruction operates on stack-local variables ([rbp-0x18] and [rbp-0x10]). No heap allocation, free, or metadata manipulation occurs. Therefore no heap primitive can be derived from BUG-002.
